title: Monitor pipeline runs - Microsoft Fabric
summary: Walks through the operational surfaces for observing Fabric Data Factory pipeline runs: the run-history flyout and monitoring hub, filtering and keyword search over activity runs, CSV export, rerun options, the Gantt view for comparing run durations, and workspace-level log monitoring via an eventhouse KQL database plus the Capacity Metrics app for capacity-level utilization.
audience: Data engineers and platform operators responsible for operating and troubleshooting Fabric pipelines in production, including metadata-driven pipelines that fan out across many parameterized runs.
why_it_matters: A metadata-driven pipeline that iterates over a control table produces many activity runs from a single pipeline definition; the monitoring hub's filtering, keyword search, and Gantt view are the mechanisms for making that fan-out observable and for diagnosing which specific iteration failed.
takeaways: Run history is reached from a pipeline's context menu and opens a flyout before linking into the fuller monitoring hub with filters.
The monitoring hub paginates past 2,000 activity runs, requiring an explicit Load more action to see the rest.
Activity runs can be filtered by status and searched by keyword across activity name, activity type, or run ID.
A failed pipeline can be rerun in full or resumed from just the failed activity, rather than always restarting from the beginning.
Workspace-level monitoring routes pipeline events into a KQL database in an eventhouse, and capacity-level consumption is tracked separately through the Fabric Capacity Metrics app.

claims.text: Pipeline run history is accessed from the pipeline's More options menu in the workspace via View run history, which opens a flyout of recent runs before linking to the fuller monitoring hub.

The monitoring hub view for a pipeline run displays detailed properties such as run ID and error messages, and paginates activity runs, requiring a Load more action once a pipeline has more than 2,000 activity runs.
Activity runs in the monitoring view can be filtered by activity status and searched by keyword against activity name, activity type, or activity run ID, and the visible columns can be customized.
Monitoring data for a pipeline run can be exported to CSV directly from the monitoring hub.
A pipeline run can be rerun either in its entirety or resumed starting only from the activity that failed, rather than always requiring a full restart.

The Gantt view renders each pipeline run as a horizontal bar grouped by pipeline name, with bar length representing run duration, to make it easy to compare durations and spot overlaps or anomalies across runs.

Enabling workspace monitoring adds a monitoring eventhouse and creates a KQL database that captures pipeline-level events, including pipeline name, run status, timestamps, and system diagnostics, in a table called ItemJobEventLogs.

Once workspace monitoring is enabled, KQL queries against the monitoring eventhouse's ItemJobEventLogs table can be used to analyze success/failure trends, performance metrics, and error details across pipeline runs.

Capacity administrators can use the separate Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics app to view how much CPU, processing time, and memory pipelines and other items consume within a capacity, to identify overload causes and peak-demand periods.
